what: The campaign raid of raid-steps.json at its busiest, a view at every step of the rules (ten a battle second), as AAirBattle::Feed takes them in a live raid: Germany's day raid on Hampshire, 1942, battle seconds 285 to 331 of tools/air-record/live-steps.ts's recording (seed 11). For Tools/air_show/air_smooth_probe --shake, battle 290 to 330: the bombers and the strategy camera in a crowd.

agents.name: Lantern
agents.will: Reports every army in the province and the provinces around it: each corps, its kind and its strength. In the province itself the agent also reports what is on order there and which air fleets are based there, and your armies attack it harder for knowing its defences.

work.label: Watch and report
work.text: Reports every army in the province and the provinces around it: each corps, its kind and its strength. In the province itself the agent also reports what is on order there and which air fleets are based there, and your armies attack it harder for knowing its defences.

work.label: Read the books
work.text: In a capital: the government's treasury and income, the true size of its army, what it has on order, what its laboratories are working on and what is in its depots.

work.label: Wreck a factory
work.text: One working factory is put out of action until engineers rebuild it. Tried once, next month, and then the agent must lie low.

work.label: Cut the railway
work.text: The track is blown. No train runs through the province until engineers relay it. Tried once, next month, and then the agent must lie low.

work.label: Fire the oilfield
work.text: The wells are set alight: the field gives 50% of its oil for 3 months. Tried once, next month, and then the agent must lie low.
work.why: There is no oilfield at London.

work.label: Wreck the airfield
work.text: Runways cratered and the fuel dump set alight: every enemy air group based on the field is grounded for the month. Tried once, next month, and then the agent must lie low.
work.why: No enemy air group flies from London.

work.label: Steal the orders
work.text: Next month's orders of the bomber groups on this field: which groups, how many bombers, the target, by day or by night. Tried each month the agent stays on it. A stolen order is never false; the gamble is in getting it.
work.why: No enemy bomber group flies from London.

desks.name: Research
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN RESEARCH
desks.tip: Your advisers keep every research team at work, on the projects a general staff would put first. You can take it back in any month.

desks.name: Building and trade
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN BUILDING AND TRADE
desks.tip: Your staff raises new corps, puts guns round industry that has been bombed, builds in your towns and signs trade agreements, inside the share of the treasury you allow it. You can take it back in any month.

desks.name: Diplomacy
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN DIPLOMACY
desks.tip: Your envoys court the neutral most ready to listen, month by month. Declaring war is always yours. You can take it back in any month.

desks.name: The secret service
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN THE SECRET SERVICE
desks.tip: The service recruits agents, sends them to watch the enemy's front and to read the books in his capital, and keeps a guard at home. It tries no sabotage. Once it has an agent to spare it also keeps a hunter where the enemy's watchers are likeliest (where his divisions mass on your front, or on the coast facing him), calling one home if it must, and it deals with every enemy agent that is uncovered: it turns one into a double agent where it can, and arrests the rest. You can take it back in any month.

desks.name: The air war
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN THE AIR WAR
desks.tip: Your air staff plans and flies the raids: factories, railways, and the enemy's troops where your armies are fighting. Your fighters meet enemy raids either way. You can take it back in any month.

desks.name: The navy and convoys
desks.label: LET MY STAFF RUN THE NAVY AND CONVOYS
desks.tip: Your admirals send the fleets out: they hunt the enemy's ships, guard your shipping lanes, shell the coasts your army stands beside and fly the carriers' strikes. Landings are always yours. You can take it back in any month.

arms.label: Infantry
arms.role: Holds ground better than it takes it. With tanks beside it, it is worth up to 15% more.

arms.label: Motorised
arms.role: Infantry on wheels: quick off the roads, and it counts as the infantry tanks need beside them.
arms.poor: forest (attack −10%); mountains (attack −25%, defence −10%, slow to enter); marsh (attack −20%, defence −10%, slow to enter)

arms.label: Armor
arms.role: The hardest hitter there is. With infantry beside it, it is worth up to 10% more; alone in a city or a forest it is worth less.
arms.poor: forest (attack −20%, defence −15%, slow to enter); hills (attack −10%); mountains (attack −40%, defence −25%, slow to enter); marsh (attack −40%, defence −25%, slow to enter); cities (attack −40%); the highest mountains (cannot enter)

arms.label: Cavalry
arms.role: Quick and light: for scouting and pursuit, not for a stand-up fight.

arms.label: Mountain
arms.role: At home in hills and mountains, where everyone else struggles.

arms.label: Fortress
arms.role: A fortress garrison: it holds its works and does not march.

arms.label: Artillery
arms.role: Massed guns. Against forts and dug-in troops, up to 2 artillery corps join an attack without taking room on the roads, and their fire wears the works down. Guns cannot take ground alone.
arms.poor: mountains (attack −20%, slow to enter); marsh (attack −20%, slow to enter)

arms.label: Engineers
arms.role: Builds and breaches: bridges, fieldworks, minefields and railways. It is not there for its rifles. Engineers cannot take ground alone.
